sanskrit: vanaṃ gate dharmapare rāme ramayatāṃ vare kausalyā rudatī svārtā bhartāram idam abravīt
english: When Rāma, the foremost of the righteous and the finest of those who bring delight, had gone to the forest, Kausalyā, weeping and overcome with grief, spoke thus to her husband.

sanskrit: yady apitriṣu lokeṣu prathitaṃ te mayad yaśaḥ sānukrośo vadānyaś ca priyavādī ca rāghavaḥ
english: 'Even in worlds other than this, your glory is proclaimed — that Rāghava is compassionate, generous, and speaks kindly.

sanskrit: kathaṃ naravaraśreṣṭha putrau tau saha sītayā duḥkhitau sukhasaṃvṛddhau vane duḥkhaṃ sahiṣyataḥ
english: How, O best of noble men, will those two sons, raised in comfort, bear hardship in the forest together with Sītā, now wretched?

sanskrit: sā nūnaṃ taruṇī śyāmā sukumārī sukhocitā katham uṣṇaṃ ca śītaṃ ca maithilī prasahiṣyate
english: She, the Maithilī, is young, dark-complexioned, delicate, and accustomed only to comfort — how will she endure heat and cold?

sanskrit: bhuktvāśanaṃ viśālākṣī sūpadaṃśānvitaṃ śubham vanyaṃ naivāram āhāraṃ kathaṃ sītopabhokṣyate
english: Having eaten fine food accompanied by savory condiments, how will wide-eyed Sītā subsist on forest fare — uncooked roots and fruits?

sanskrit: gītavāditranirghoṣaṃ śrutvā śubham aninditā kathaṃ kravyādasiṃhānāṃ śabdaṃ śroṣyaty aśobhanam
english: She who has heard only the auspicious sounds of song and music — how will that blameless one bear hearing the dreadful roars of flesh-eating lions?

sanskrit: mahendradhvajasaṃkāśaḥ kva nu śete mahābhujaḥ bhujaṃ parighasaṃkāśam upadhāya mahābalaḥ
english: Where now does he sleep — he of great arms, resembling Mahendra's banner, resting his arm that is like an iron bar, he of mighty strength?

sanskrit: padmavarṇaṃ sukeśāntaṃ padmaniḥśvāsam uttamam kadā drakṣyāmi rāmasya vadanaṃ puṣkarekṣaṇam
english: When shall I again behold Rāma's face — lotus-hued, with beautiful hair at its end, fragrant as a lotus-breath, the finest of faces, with lotus eyes?

sanskrit: vajrasāramayaṃ nūnaṃ hṛdayaṃ me na saṃśayaḥ apaśyantyā na taṃ yad vai phalatīdaṃ sahasradhā
english: My heart is surely made of the essence of adamant — there is no doubt — since, not seeing him, it does not shatter into a thousand pieces.

sanskrit: yadi pañcadaśe varṣe rāghavaḥ punar eṣyati jahyād rājyaṃ ca kośaṃ ca bharatenopabhokṣyate
english: If after fifteen years Rāghava returns, will he renounce the kingdom and the treasury that Bharata has been enjoying?

sanskrit: evaṃ kanīyasā bhrātrā bhuktaṃ rājyaṃ viśāṃ pate bhrātā jyeṣṭhā variṣṭhāś ca kimarthaṃ nāvamaṃsyate
english: O lord of the people, a kingdom once enjoyed by a younger brother — why would an elder brother, who is the most worthy, not disdain it?

sanskrit: na pareṇāhṛtaṃ bhakṣyaṃ vyāghraḥ khāditum icchati evam eva naravyāghraḥ paralīḍhaṃ na maṃsyate
english: A tiger does not wish to eat prey that has been seized by another; in the same way, this tiger among men will not accept what has already been licked by another.

sanskrit: havir ājyaṃ puroḍāśāḥ kuśā yūpāś ca khādirāḥ naitāni yātayāmāni kurvanti punar adhvare
english: Oblations, clarified butter, sacrificial cakes, kuśa grass, and posts of khadira wood — once used, these are not employed again in a sacrifice.

sanskrit: tathā hy āttam idaṃ rājyaṃ hṛtasārāṃ surām iva nābhimantum alaṃ rāmo naṣṭasomam ivādhvaram
english: Likewise, this kingdom — once appropriated — Rāma will not consecrate, just as one does not reconsecrate liquor stripped of its essence, or a sacrifice from which the Soma is lost.

sanskrit: naivaṃvidham asatkāraṃ rāghavo marṣayiṣyati balavān iva śārdūlo bāladher abhimarśanam
english: Rāghava will not tolerate such an insult, just as a powerful tiger will not endure the touch of a child's hand.

sanskrit: sa tādṛśaḥ siṃhabalo vṛṣabhākṣo nararṣabhaḥ svayam eva hataḥ pitrā jalajenātmajo yathā
english: He of such lion-like strength, bull-eyed, that bull among men — he has been slain by his own father, as a lotus-born son might be slain by a river.

sanskrit: dvijāti carito dharmaḥ śāstradṛṣṭaḥ sanātanaḥ yadi te dharmanirate tvayā putre vivāsite
english: The eternal duty taught by scripture and practiced by the twice-born — if you are devoted to dharma, was it thus when you banished your son?

sanskrit: gatir evāk patir nāryā dvitīyā gatir ātmajaḥ tṛtīyā jñātayo rājaṃś caturthī neha vidyate
english: The husband is the foremost refuge of a woman; the son is her second; kinsmen are the third — O king, there is no fourth in this world.

sanskrit: tatra tvaṃ caiva me nāsti rāmaś ca vanam āśritaḥ na vanaṃ gantum icchāmi sarvathā hi hatā tvayā
english: Of these, you are lost to me, and Rāma has taken to the forest. I have no wish to go to the forest either — for you have utterly destroyed me in every way.

sanskrit: hataṃ tvayā rājyam idaṃ sarāṣṭraṃ hatas tathātmā saha mantribhiś ca hatā saputrāsmi hatāś ca paurāḥ sutaś ca bhāryā ca tava prahṛṣṭau
english: By you this kingdom with its realm has been ruined, so too your very self along with your ministers; I am destroyed with my son, and the citizens are destroyed — while your son and wife rejoice.'

sanskrit: imāṃ giraṃ dāruṇaśabdasaṃśritāṃ niśamya rājāpi mumoha duḥkhitaḥ tataḥ sa śokaṃ praviveśa pārthivaḥ svaduṣkṛtaṃ cāpi punas tadāsmarat
english: Hearing these words filled with such harsh sounds, the king fainted in his grief. Then that lord of the earth plunged deeper into sorrow, and once again he recalled his own past sin.

sanskrit: evaṃ tu kruddhayā rājā rāmamātrā saśokayā śrāvitaḥ paruṣaṃ vākyaṃ cintayām āsa duḥkhitaḥ
english: Thus made to hear harsh words by Rāma's mother, who was both angry and grief-stricken, the king fell into sorrowful reflection.

sanskrit: tasya cintayamānasya pratyabhāt karma duṣkṛtam yad anena kṛtaṃ pūrvam ajñānāc chabdavedhinā
english: As he reflected, there rose before him the evil deed he had committed long ago in ignorance — when he had shot by sound alone.

sanskrit: amanās tena śokena rāmaśokena ca prabhuḥ dahyamānas tu śokābhyāṃ kausalyām āha bhūpatiḥ
english: His mind undone by that grief and by grief for Rāma, burning with both sorrows, that master, the lord of the earth, spoke to Kausalyā.

sanskrit: prasādaye tvāṃ kausalye racito 'yaṃ mayāñjaliḥ vatsalā cānṛśaṃsā ca tvaṃ hi nityaṃ pareṣv api
english: 'I beg your grace, Kausalyā — I fold my hands before you. You are always gentle and without cruelty, even toward strangers.

sanskrit: bhartā tu khalu nārīṇāṃ guṇavān nirguṇo 'pi vā dharmaṃ vimṛśamānānāṃ pratyakṣaṃ devi daivatam
english: Surely the husband — whether possessed of virtues or devoid of them — is, for women who reflect on dharma, the very visible deity, O queen.

sanskrit: sā tvaṃ dharmaparā nityaṃ dṛṣṭalokaparāvara nārhase vipriyaṃ vaktuṃ duḥkhitāpi suduḥkhitam
english: You who are ever devoted to dharma, who have seen the ways of this world and the next — even in your great grief you ought not speak harshly to one who is himself deeply afflicted.'

sanskrit: tad vākyaṃ karuṇaṃ rājñaḥ śrutvā dīnasya bhāṣitam kausalyā vyasṛjad bāṣpaṃ praṇālīva navodakam
english: Hearing those piteous, compassionate words of the wretched king, Kausalyā shed tears like a watercourse releasing fresh water.

sanskrit: sa mūdrhṇi baddhvā rudatī rājñaḥ padmam ivāñjalim saṃbhramād abravīt trastā tvaramāṇākṣaraṃ vacaḥ
english: Weeping, she joined her palms like a lotus and held them to her head before the king; then, frightened and agitated, she spoke words in quick succession.

sanskrit: prasīda śirasā yāce bhūmau nitatitāsmi te yācitāsmi hatā deva hantavyāhaṃ na hi tvayā
english: 'Be gracious — I beg you with my head bowed to the ground. I am wretched in my asking, O lord; I am not one who should be destroyed by you.

sanskrit: naiṣā hi sā strī bhavati ślāghanīyena dhīmatā ubhayor lokayor vīra patyā yā saṃprasādyate
english: She is not truly a woman worthy of praise by a wise man in either world, O hero, who must be won over by her husband with supplication.

sanskrit: jānāmi dharmaṃ dharmajña tvāṃ jāne satyavādinam putraśokārtayā tat tu mayā kim api bhāṣitam
english: I know dharma, and O knower of dharma, I know you to be a speaker of truth. Whatever I said was said by me while overcome with grief for my son.'

sanskrit: śoko nāśayate dhairyaṃ śoko nāśayate śrutam śoko nāśayate sarvaṃ nāsti śokasamo ripuḥ
english: Grief destroys courage; grief destroys learning; grief destroys everything. There is no enemy equal to grief.

sanskrit: śayam āpatitaḥ soḍhuṃ praharo ripuhastataḥ soḍhum āpatitaḥ śokaḥ susūkṣmo 'pi na śakyate
english: A blow falling from an enemy's hand can be endured; but grief, even the most subtle, when it falls cannot be borne.

sanskrit: vanavāsāya rāmasya pañcarātro 'dya gaṇyate yaḥ śokahataharṣāyāḥ pañcavarṣopamo mama
english: Today marks five nights of Rāma's forest exile — yet for me, whose joy is shattered by grief, it seems the equal of five years.

sanskrit: taṃ hi cintayamānāyāḥ śoko 'yaṃ hṛdi vardhate adīnām iva vegena samudrasalilaṃ mahat
english: As I think of him, this grief swells in my heart with the force with which the vast waters of the ocean rise unchecked.

sanskrit: evaṃ hi kathayantyās tu kausalyāyāḥ śubhaṃ vacaḥ mandaraśmir abhūt suryo rajanī cābhyavartata
english: While Kausalyā was thus speaking these worthy words, the sun's rays grew dim and night drew near.

sanskrit: atha prahlādito vākyair devyā kausalyayā nṛpaḥ śokena ca samākrānto nidrāyā vaśam eyivān
english: Then the king, somewhat comforted by the words of Queen Kausalyā yet overcome by sorrow, fell under the sway of sleep.

sanskrit: pratibuddho muhur tena śokopahatacetanaḥ atha rājā daśarathaḥ sa cintām abhyapadyata
english: Awakening repeatedly, his mind shattered by grief, King Daśaratha then fell into sorrowful thought.

sanskrit: rāmalakṣmaṇayoś caiva vivāsād vāsavopamam āviveśopasargas taṃ tamaḥ sūryam ivāsuram
english: By reason of the banishment of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, a calamity seized that man equal to Vāsava, as darkness seizes the sun at the time of a demon's eclipse.

sanskrit: sa rājā rajanīṃ ṣaṣṭhīṃ rāme pravrajite vanam ardharātre daśarathaḥ saṃsmaran duṣkṛtaṃ kṛtam kausalyāṃ putraśokārtām idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: That king Daśaratha, on the sixth night after Rāma had gone forth to the forest, at midnight, recalling the evil deed he had done, spoke these words to Kausalyā, who was afflicted by grief for her son.

sanskrit: yad ācarati kalyāṇi śubhaṃ vā yadi vāśubham tad eva labhate bhadre kartā karmajam ātmanaḥ
english: 'O auspicious one, whatever a person does — whether good or evil — that very fruit born of the act he himself receives, O blessed one.

sanskrit: guru lāghavam arthānām ārambhe karmaṇāṃ phalam doṣaṃ vā yo na jānāti sa bāla iti hocyate
english: One who, at the commencement of actions, does not know the weight or lightness of purposes, nor the fruit, nor the fault — such a one is called a child.

sanskrit: kaś cid āmravaṇaṃ chittvā palāśāṃś ca niṣiñcati puṣpaṃ dṛṣṭvā phale gṛdhnuḥ sa śocati phalāgame
english: Someone cuts down a mango grove and instead waters palāśa trees; greedy at the sight of blossoms, he repents when the fruit-time comes.

sanskrit: so 'ham āmravaṇaṃ chittvā palāśāṃś ca nyaṣecayam rāmaṃ phalāgame tyaktvā paścāc chocāmi durmatiḥ
english: That am I — I cut down the mango grove and watered the palāśa trees; having abandoned Rāma when the fruit-time came, I now repent in my foolishness.

sanskrit: labdhaśabdena kausalye kumāreṇa dhanuṣmatā kumāraḥ śabdavedhīti mayā pāpam idaṃ kṛtam tad idaṃ me 'nusaṃprāptaṃ devi duḥkhaṃ svayaṃ kṛtam
english: O Kausalyā, when I was a young man just gaining fame as an archer, this sin was committed by me — with a bow I shot at a sound I could not see; and now, O queen, this self-made sorrow has come upon me.

sanskrit: saṃmohād iha bālena yathā syād bhakṣitaṃ viṣam evaṃ mamāpy avijñātaṃ śabdavedhyamayaṃ phalam
english: As a child in confusion might swallow poison, so too by me unknowingly the fruit of shooting by sound alone has been consumed.

sanskrit: devy anūḍhā tvam abhavo yuvarājo bhavāmy aham tataḥ prāvṛḍ anuprāptā madakāmavivardhinī
english: O queen, you were as yet unwed; I had just become crown prince; then the rains arrived, that season which swells passion and desire.

sanskrit: upāsyahi rasān bhaumāṃs taptvā ca jagad aṃśubhiḥ paretācaritāṃ bhīmāṃ ravir āviśate diśam
english: Having drawn up the earthly waters and scorched the world with his rays, the sun now entered the dreadful quarter where the dead journey.

sanskrit: uṣṇam antardadhe sadyaḥ snigdhā dadṛśire ghanāḥ tato jahṛṣire sarve bhekasāraṅgabarhiṇaḥ
english: The heat immediately subsided; moist clouds appeared; and thereupon all frogs, spotted deer, and peacocks rejoiced.

sanskrit: patitenāmbhasā channaḥ patamānena cāsakṛt ābabhau mattasāraṅgas toyarāśir ivācalaḥ
english: Covered repeatedly by water falling and still falling, the spotted deer blazed with intoxication like a mountain covered with a mass of water.

sanskrit: tasminn atisukhe kāle dhanuṣmān iṣumān rathī vyāyāma kṛtasaṃkalpaḥ sarayūm anvagāṃ nadīm
english: In that most pleasant season, armed with bow and arrows, mounted in my chariot, resolved on exercise, I followed the Sarayū river.

sanskrit: nipāne mahiṣaṃ rātrau gajaṃ vābhyāgataṃ nadīm anyaṃ vā śvāpadaṃ kaṃ cij jighāṃsur ajitendriyaḥ
english: Wishing to slay a buffalo, an elephant, or some other wild beast that might come to the watering-place at night, with my senses still untamed.

sanskrit: athāndhakāre tv aśrauṣaṃ jale kumbhasya paryataḥ acakṣur viṣaye ghoṣaṃ vāraṇasyeva nardataḥ
english: Then in the darkness I heard the sound of a pot being filled in the water, like the trumpeting of an elephant beyond the range of sight.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ śaram uddhṛtya dīptam āśīviṣopamam amuñcaṃ niśitaṃ bāṇam aham āśīviṣopamam
english: Then I drew a blazing arrow, like a venomous serpent, and released that sharp shaft.

sanskrit: tatra vāg uṣasi vyaktā prādurāsīd vanaukasaḥ hā heti patatas toye vāg abhūt tatra mānuṣī katham asmadvidhe śastraṃ nipatet tu tapasvini
english: Then a clear voice arose from the forest-dweller — 'Alas!' as he fell into the water; it was a human voice there: 'How could a weapon fall upon a suffering ascetic such as I?'

sanskrit: praviviktāṃ nadīṃ rātrāv udāhāro 'ham āgataḥ iṣuṇābhihataḥ kena kasya vā kiṃ kṛtaṃ mayā
english: 'I came alone at night to this solitary river to draw water. By whose arrow am I struck? Whose enemy am I? What have I done?'

sanskrit: ṛṣer hi nyasta daṇḍasya vane vanyena jīvataḥ kathaṃ nu śastreṇa vadho madvidhasya vidhīyate
english: 'How can the killing by a weapon be ordained for one such as I — an ascetic who has laid aside the staff, who lives in the forest on forest fare?'

sanskrit: jaṭābhāradharasyaiva valkalājinavāsasaḥ ko vadhena mamārthī syāt kiṃ vāsyāpakṛtaṃ mayā
english: 'One who bears the weight of matted locks, clad in bark and deer-skin — who could wish to slay me? What wrong have I done to anyone?'

sanskrit: evaṃ niṣphalam ārabdhaṃ kevalānarthasaṃhitam na kaś cit sādhu manyeta yathaiva gurutalpagam
english: 'Such a deed, undertaken in vain, bringing only harm — no one would approve it, even as no one approves one who violates his teacher's bed.'

sanskrit: nemaṃ tathānuśocāmi jīvitakṣayam ātmanaḥ mātaraṃ pitaraṃ cobhāv anuśocāmi madvidhe
english: 'I do not grieve so much for my own loss of life; it is for both my mother and father that I grieve — for those like me.'

sanskrit: tad etān mithunaṃ vṛddhaṃ cirakālabhṛtaṃ mayā mayi pañcatvam āpanne kāṃ vṛttiṃ vartayiṣyati
english: 'That aged pair, long sustained by me — when I have gone to the five elements, how will they live?'

sanskrit: vṛddhau ca mātāpitarāv ahaṃ caikeṣuṇā hataḥ kena sma nihatāḥ sarve subālenākṛtātmanā
english: 'Both aged parents, and I slain by a single arrow — we are all destroyed by some utter child, one of unformed self.'

sanskrit: taṃ giraṃ karuṇāṃ śrutvā mama dharmānukāṅkṣiṇaḥ karābhyāṃ saśaraṃ cāpaṃ vyathitasyāpatad bhuvi
english: Hearing those piteous words of that lover of dharma, my bow with its arrow fell from my stricken hands to the ground.

sanskrit: taṃ deśam aham āgamya dīnasattvaḥ sudurmanāḥ apaśyam iṣuṇā tīre sarayvās tāpasaṃ hatam
english: Coming to that spot, wretched in spirit and deeply sorrowful, I saw the ascetic lying wounded by my arrow on the bank of the Sarayū.

sanskrit: sa mām udvīkṣya netrābhyāṃ trastam asvasthacetasaṃ ity uvāca vacaḥ krūraṃ didhakṣann iva tejasā
english: He looked up at me with both eyes — I was terrified, my mind in disorder — and spoke harsh words, as though burning me with his energy.

sanskrit: kiṃ tavāpakṛtaṃ rājan vane nivasatā mayā jihīrṣur ambho gurvarthaṃ yad ahaṃ tāḍitas tvayā
english: 'What wrong have I done you, O king? I who dwell in the forest, who came here seeking water for my teacher's sake — why have you struck me?'

sanskrit: ekena khalu bāṇena marmaṇy abhihate mayi dvāv andhau nihatau vṛddhau mātā janayitā ca me
english: 'By a single arrow that has struck my vital spot, two blind old ones are slain — my mother and my father.'

sanskrit: tau nūnaṃ durbalāv andhau matpratīkṣau pipāsitau ciram āśākṛtāṃ tṛṣṇāṃ kaṣṭāṃ saṃdhārayiṣyataḥ
english: 'Those two, surely weak and blind, waiting for me, thirsting — they will long endure that terrible, hope-begotten thirst.'

sanskrit: na nūnaṃ tapaso vāsti phalayogaḥ śrutasya vā pitā yan māṃ na jānāti śayānaṃ patitaṃ bhuvi
english: 'Surely there is no fruit of asceticism or of sacred learning, since my father does not know that I lie fallen on the ground.'

sanskrit: jānann api ca kiṃ kuryād aśaktir aparikramaḥ bhidyamānam ivāśaktas trātum anyo nago nagam
english: 'And even if he knew, what could he do — he who is without power, unable to move, like one tree unable to save another that is being felled?'

sanskrit: pitus tvam eva me gatvā śīghram ācakṣva rāghava na tvām anudahet kruddho vanaṃ vahnir ivaidhitaḥ
english: 'Go quickly yourself to my father and tell him, O Rāghava; in his anger he will not burn you up like a blazing fire consuming a forest.'

sanskrit: iyam ekapadī rājan yato me pitur āśramaḥ taṃ prasādaya gatvā tvaṃ na tvāṃ sa kupitaḥ śapet
english: 'This single path, O king, leads to where my father's hermitage is. Go there and propitiate him; even though angry, he will not curse you.'

sanskrit: viśalyaṃ kuru māṃ rājan marma me niśitaḥ śaraḥ ruṇaddhi mṛdu sotsedhaṃ tīram amburayo yathā
english: 'Remove the arrow from me, O king; the sharp shaft blocks my vital spot, causing swelling and pain, like a flood-current stopping up a soft riverbank.'

sanskrit: na dvijātir ahaṃ rājan mā bhūt te manaso vyathā śūdrāyām asmi vaiśyena jāto janapadādhipa
english: 'I am not a twice-born, O king — let there be no anguish in your mind. I was born of a Vaiśya father upon a Śūdra woman, O lord of the land.'

sanskrit: itīva vadataḥ kṛcchrād bāṇābhihatamarmaṇaḥ tasya tv ānamyamānasya taṃ bāṇam aham uddharam
english: As he was speaking thus with difficulty — his vital spot struck by the arrow, his body bending — I drew out that arrow.

sanskrit: jalārdragātraṃ tu vilapya kṛcchān marmavraṇaṃ saṃtatam ucchasantam tataḥ sarayvāṃ tam ahaṃ śayānaṃ samīkṣya bhadre subhṛśaṃ viṣaṇṇaḥ
english: His body wet with water, lamenting with difficulty, his vital wound unceasing, still breathing — then, O blessed one, seeing him lying on the bank of the Sarayū, I was overcome with the deepest anguish.
